questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=1.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=-1.$ This means that $k=1.5$ and $b=-1,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x-(-1)}+1.5=\frac{a}{x+1}+1.5.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(1,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x+1}+1.5 \\ 3.5 & =\frac{a}{1+1}+1.5 \\ 2 & =\frac{a}{2} \\ a & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

                    Graphing a Transformed Reciprocal Function
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To plot $y = -\dfrac{2}{x-1}-1,$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/9da0db2e6c97e507e82b7ca801e46802fabf91ad31ff53ad3cc9ae580151370a.png)

- Translate it by one unit to the right to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{x-1}.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/8ce8c53f202f04b3b34a247b797f65f7616e8772afa1751de126ddd401417bd7.png)

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{2}{x-1}.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Solving for Some Unknowns Given the Graph of a Transformed Reciprocal Function
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/fb46d056a8d8010eca509543c231c875f4980a21f1af17505fa98c8c64106207.png)

The diagram above shows the graph of $y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What is the value of $a+b+k?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=-1,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=2.$ This means that $k=-1$ and $b=2,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y = \dfrac{a}{x-2}+(-1) = \dfrac{a}{x-2}-1.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(3,2)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x-2}-1 \\ 2 & =\frac{a}{3-2}-1 \\ 3 & =\frac{a}{1} \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+b+k = 3+2+(-1) = 4.$

tutorials.name: Applying a Stretch With a Scale Factor Less Than One
tutorials.problem:
Similarly, to sketch the graph of $y=\dfrac{1}{2x},$ we take the graph of $y=\dfrac1x$ and stretch it by a scale factor of $\dfrac12$ parallel to the $y$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244490/assets/08c02826d4c2dff684e00c01e9229e5ef7767f4122d99fcfa8e5d63c254cbd94.png)

Note the following:

- The point $(1,1)$ on $y=\dfrac1x$ is mapped to the point $\left(1,\dfrac12\right)$ on $y=\dfrac{1}{2x}.$

- The point $(-1,-1)$ on $y=\dfrac1x$ is mapped to the point $\left(-1,-\dfrac12\right)$ on $y=\dfrac{1}{2x}.$
